look_here_first: First stroke/look at a LOWER STEM 10–20 cm above plant base: S. gigantea is often smooth (GLABROUS) and sometimes waxy bluish (GLAUCOUS) well below flower panicle. The leaves are narrow lanceolate and often 3-nerved, but ALL tall-goldenrod complex relatives can share 3 veins. Compare hairier lower stems on altissima and canadensis, moisture settings as support, then measure phyllaries if uncertain. Never use only flower plume or leaf veins.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — project Hays-local source pool. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index includes Solidago gigantea. Williamson — dedicated county flora documents S. gigantea.

best_field_traits: lower stem glabrous to nearly glabrous
often moist riparian or mesic sites
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with S. altissima, the lower stem is much smoother and less hairy. Compared with S. juliae, S. gigantea is more strongly rhizomatous and typically has smoother stems with narrower leaves.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.first: Smooth lower stem and leaf UNDERSIDE

key.gigantea: Smooth/hairless to near-hairless, often whitish-blue waxy
key.canadensis: Generally hairy but can become nearly smooth toward base

key.gigantea: Narrow lanceolate and 3 veins; relatively smooth lower surface
key.altissima: Firm and slightly rough, three veins; upper margin often fewer teeth
key.canadensis: Often finer and more regular serrations, three veins

key.altissima: Also broad plume; can't prove giant from flowers alone

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: GIANT = GLABROUS lower stem (then leaf underside). TALL/CANADA = commonly hairy below, but check other evidence.
